newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN RACQUET MAKER DONNAY TURNOVER SET TO SOAR.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN RACQUET MAKER DONNAY TURNOVER SET TO SOAR.

text.p: Belgian racquet maker Donnay International, which has been bought by Britain's Sport & Ski, should see turnover soar tenfold to 5.0 billion francs (100 million stg) by 1999, CDS Holdings said on Tuesday.
Sport & Ski recently bought Donnay via U.K. group CDS Holdings for 125 million Belgian francs (2.5 million stg) from southern Belgium's Walloon regional government.
"We're confident of 30 million stg turnover next year - three times what they're doing now," CDS Holdings chairman Stephen Nardelli told a news conference.
"We hope for over 50 million stg in 1998 and will achieve 100 million in three years comfortably," he added.
Donnay's headquarters are to remain in Couvain, southern Belgium, and a new one billion franc (20 million stg) distribution centre is planned in the area.
Nardelli said Donnay was viewed as a long term investment and future profits would be put back into the company.
